 GameNative Android PC game emulator prepares graphics fixes for Mali, PowerVR and Xclipse GPUs
 GameNative is preparing an experimental GPU wrapper for Mali, PowerVR and Samsung Xclipse devices.
 Nov 15, 14:34 GMT • WhyCry • 2 min read Set as Preferred Source Follow on Google © GameNative Updated GPU wrapper improves compatibility on Android phones 
 GameNative is preparing another update to its open-source PC gaming application for Android. This time, the developers are focusing on graphics compatibility for devices without Qualcomm Adreno GPUs. The upcoming release introduces an updated GPU wrapper with experimental fixes for ARM Mali, PowerVR and Samsung Xclipse graphics processors.
 GameNative allows Android users to run PC games from Steam, Epic Games, GOG and Amazon without cloud streaming. The application uses compatibility components such as DXVK and VKD3D to support Windows games. While the project already supports some non-Adreno GPUs, the developers have been working to address graphics driver limitations that prevent games from launching or displaying correctly.
 In the next GameNative update – experimental graphics fixes with our updated wrapper for non-Adreno (Mali, PowerVR, Xclipse) devices.
 If you have one of the devices (or GPUs) listed below, keep an eye out! pic.twitter.com/DEWg52Y1Lp 
 — GameNative (@GameNativeApp) November 15, 2026 
 DirectX 11 and DirectX 12 support improved across multiple GPUs 
 According to GameNative’s comparison, the updated wrapper resolves several issues affecting DXVK 2.7 and VKD3D 3.0. On older Mali devices, both translation layers previously failed to detect a compatible GPU. The new wrapper allows them to run, while also fixing OpenGL startup problems and corrupted compressed textures.
 The improvements cover a range of devices, including the Pixel 6 through Pixel 10, several Samsung Galaxy phones and tablets, and models from Motorola, OPPO and Vivo. On the Pixel 10 with PowerVR graphics, DXVK and VKD3D previously crashed, while OpenGL produced a blank screen. The developers report that all three now work, with BC7 texture decoding also fixed.
 © GameNative Samsung’s Xclipse GPUs are included as well. The Galaxy S24 with Xclipse 940 reportedly no longer crashes when running DXVK 2.7, while the Galaxy S26 with Xclipse 960 can now display textures correctly using the same translation layer. VKD3D 3.0 has not yet been tested on the Galaxy S26.
